audit.whatIsWrong: Chart gave Swain levels 2, 3, first item and 2+ items and Skill at 4-5 and 6, while every why and spike for those rows describes a Nautilus takeover, and the win rate is 62.5%.
audit.why: Packet levelChart: Skill, Nautilus, Nautilus, Nautilus, Nautilus, Nautilus, Swain. Swain has no dash and Nevermove (10-12s) is his only peel.
audit.corrected: Both layers set to Skill, Nautilus x5, Swain, with ratings flipped to match.

audit.why: Spikes: level 3 full pin, level 6 Depth Charge, first item engage window, late Swain with Liandry's/Rylai's and Demonic Ascension (flat 120s).

audit.whatIsWrong: Nevermove was described only as slow-travelling with a delay. Riot's text is more specific and more useful: the wave travels out, then RETURNS to Swain and roots what it hits on the way back. Ravenous Flock's healing and permanent max health were never stated despite two flagged interactions.
audit.why: Riot text: 'launches a wave of demonic power forward. It then returns to Swain and roots enemies it hits'; passive: 'ravens collect Soul Fragments that heal him and permanently increase his maximum health'. Vision of Empire also grants a Soul Fragment when it hits a champion.
audit.corrected: Dodge Nevermove twice — the root is on the return — then punish its 10-12s cooldown. Bring Grievous Wounds and MR, not armour: his healing and max-health growth are what beat a tank's chip damage.

edits.before: - Swain Demonic Ascension: matchup-defining — His drain. Chain CC when it’s down. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Swain Demonic Ascension: a flat 120s drain — chain your CC inside that window. - Nevermove: 10-12s, roots on the return wave and is his only peel. - Depth Charge: the win condition — kill windows only.

edits.before: Level 1 is roughly even — you have no all-in without W/E, and his Q (Death's Hand) bolts out-poke you if you stand in lane trading autos for free. But the moment you hit Level 3 with Dredge Line, Titan's Wrath and Riptide, you own it: bait or dodge his E (Nevermove) — it has a slow travel and a delay, so sidestep it, then immediately Q-pull him, weave your passive root, and W-splash him down. His E is his only peel; if it misses or is on cooldown, he has zero escape from your anchor.
edits.after: Level 1 is roughly even — you have no all-in without W/E, and his Q (Death's Hand) bolts out-poke you if you stand in lane trading autos for free. But the moment you hit Level 3 with Dredge Line, Titan's Wrath and Riptide, you own it: dodge Nevermove twice, because it roots on the RETURN wave and not on the way out, then Q-pull him, weave your passive root and W-splash him down. It is his only peel, on 10-12 seconds; if it misses he has zero escape from your anchor.

notes: Only 8 games behind the 62.5% win rate, but the packet chart, the kits and the existing prose all agree Nautilus owns levels 2 through first item, so the chart was flipped to them. Vision of Empire's Soul Fragment on champion hit is now reflected in the anti-heal advice.
